provenance.instrument: Whitemarsh Township Code Chapter 116 Zoning (Ord. No. 112, 9-26-1957, amended in its entirety by Ord. No. 409, 6-18-1981, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 code date 2025-04-10 (breadcrumb). Chapter 116 New Laws on 2026-11-14: Ord. No. 1049 (2026-01-08), Zoning Amendment, shown only as a PDF and not read. Ord. No. 1049 (2026-01-08), not yet codified, was read on 2026-11-26: it amends 116-11 definitions, 116-168 average lot area by steep slope ratio (lots in a conservation design subdivision under Article XXXVI stay exempt) and 116-169 steep slope disturbance limits. It does not touch 116-272E or any use list.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 breadcrumb 'Code 2025-04-10'. Ord. No. 1049 (Zoning Amendment, adopted 2026-01-08) is listed under New Laws for Chapter 116 and is not yet in the code text.
checks: The code's accessory dwelling unit is tied to a conservation design subdivision: 'Accessory dwelling units (ADU) including, but not limited to, elder cottages for relatives and tenant houses for employees of a farm or estate and proposed in Option One subdivisions, are permitted within the Conservation Overlay Design District' (116-272E, 116-11)

Option One is a by-right conservation design option only in AAAA and AAA, inside the Conservation Design Overlay shown on the Zoning Map, with a permanent conservation easement and a density of one dwelling unit per 10 acres of base site area (116-270A(1), 116-42A, 116-46A, 116-268A). Ask the Zoning Officer whether the lot is in an Option One subdivision

Where allowed: inside the house, in an existing historic structure, or in a new structure on a tract of 15 acres or more. Tract area is all land within the site as defined by the deed (116-11), so ask whether the test is on the subdivision tract or the lot. One ADU on a lot under 10 acres, two on 10 acres or more. First ADU at most 900 sq ft gross floor area, a second 750 sq ft (1,800 on lots over 15 acres). Historic accessory buildings over 75 years old may exceed these limits (116-272E(1) to (3))

Building permits only after a restrictive conservation easement bars enlarging the ADU, more ADUs and further subdivision. Montgomery County Department of Health approval for any on-site sewage system (116-272E(4))

ADU height at most 25 ft except historic buildings. In AAA the Option One standards give accessory buildings 20 ft: conflicting text, ask (116-46A(8)(b), 116-268C more restrictive applies, 116-33.2 overlay takes precedence). The ADU stays on the same lot as the house (116-272E(5), (6))

An annual occupancy permit is needed when a dwelling is occupied by more than one family or by adults not of the principal family (116-30). An accessory structure may be occupied only while the house is (116-24D(1))

Detached accessory buildings: not in the front yard or forward of the front of the house, at least 4 ft from side and rear lines, 15 ft from the house. All accessory uses and structures together cover at most 30% of the required rear yard (116-24D(3), E(3))
A guesthouse in an accessory structure must have no kitchen and is not for rent or permanent occupancy (116-24B(9))

Conversion of a single-family dwelling into more dwelling units is a special exception anywhere: a petition signed by owners of 60% of the street frontage within 500 ft, 750 sq ft per unit, lot area per family at least 75% of the district requirement, no outside change except for safety, only for a large dwelling with relatively little economic usefulness as a single-family house (116-26)

Without public sewer and public water, lots in AAA, AA, A and B need 2 acres, the house 60 ft and accessory buildings 30 ft from the nearest property line or street, accessory buildings at most 20 ft and one story. With one of the two, 1.5 acres (116-23)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Whitemarsh Township (Montgomery County) Zoning Officer. Read on eCode360 (WH0819) in a browser, one page at a time, on 2026-11-14. Fix round 2026-11-14: read again 116-272, Article IV (116-16 to 116-33.4, incl. 116-23, 116-24, 116-30, 116-33.2), 116-268 and the tract area definition (116-11 search excerpt). The 15 acre test is now a condition, the size and height caps are held so a historic building does not show them, and 116-23A and 116-30 are added. The front-yard bar (116-24E(3)(a)) stays in checks because the tool hides the district front yard on lots outside the ADU scope when the envelope flag is set. Code search (all content, New Laws included) for 'accessory dwelling', 'accessory apartment', 'in-law', ECHO, granny, 'family dwelling', relative, caretaker, 'housekeeping unit', 'guest house', 'accessory unit' and 'living quarters' found the ADU definition (116-11), the Conservation Design Overlay ADU (116-272E), quarters of a household employee, caretaker or watchman (116-24B(14)), conversions (116-26) and a caretaker residence in HVY (116-155). Searches for two-family, duplex, conversion and historic structures found 116-26, the SM-MU and VC use lists and 116-293 (VC historic building reuse, no dwelling path). Use lists read: AAAA to B (116-35), AD (116-74), SM-MU (116-310), VC (116-290). TDO bars single-family and two-family dwellings (116-318, search excerpt). Use lists not read: LR and HR, MHP, CR, AR, CLI, CLI-X, LIM, HVY, EX, CCRC and the Institutional and Recreational overlays. The definition of residential districts names a C Residential District, but Article XI is reserved. Second reading 2026-11-26 (G0): Ord. No. 1049 PDF read (steep slopes, 116-11, 116-168, 116-169; no ADU or use-list text); its slope disturbance limits added as a condition. A full-text search of the Chapter 116 print view finds 'accessory dwelling unit' only in the 116-11 definition and the Option One ADU rule, and no elder cottage, tenant house, accessory apartment or in-law unit in any other district's use list, so the unread use lists (LR/HR, MHP, CR, AR, industrial, EX, CCRC) hold no ADU path. Left as disputes the code does not settle: tract against lot for the 15-acre test, AAA accessory height 20 ft (116-268C) against the 25 ft ADU height (116-33.2 overlay precedence), and the 116-23A 30 ft accessory yards without public sewer and water (said as a condition).

term.note: 'A building or portion thereof providing complete housekeeping facilities for one family as permitted within a conservation design subdivision or land development' (Ord. No. 812, 2006).

status.note: Permitted in the Conservation Design Overlay, in Option One subdivisions only (AAAA and AAA). Option One is one of three 'by-right development options'. Elsewhere the code has no ADU rule.

scope_districts.note: 'Option One is permitted in AAAA and AAA Residential Districts only.' The overlay covers parts of AAAA, AAA, AA and A as shown on the Zoning Map (116-268A).

status_outside.note: Outside an Option One subdivision a lot in AAAA to B allows 'One single-family detached dwelling' and accessory uses.

path.note: Option One is a 'by-right development option'. Building permits for the ADU follow a recorded conservation easement.

fallback_path.note: Relief from a district rule is a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

value.name: Conversion of a single-family dwelling to more families
value.conditions: A petition signed by owners of 60% or more of the street frontage within 500 ft. Each dwelling unit at least 750 sq ft of floor area. Lot area per family at least 75% of the district requirement. Yards and building area not reduced. No outside change except for safety. The Board sets the number of families. Parking met.

requires.condition: A large dwelling with relatively little economic usefulness as a conforming use
A petition signed by owners of 60% or more of the frontage on the same street within 500 ft

value.note: Lot figures are for two families at 75% of the district lot area per family. The section names no district.

value.name: Two-family dwelling in SM-MU
value.conditions: Single-family and two-family dwellings are permitted uses. Lot 6,000 sq ft detached, width 40 ft, front 10 ft, side 10 ft, rear 30 ft, 35 ft and 2 stories.
value.note: Read as a path for an existing house converted to two units.

value.name: Two-family residence or multifamily conversion of up to four units in VC
value.conditions: 'Two-family residence' and 'Multifamily conversion; no more than four units' are permitted uses. Conditions for all uses in 116-291 apply.
value.note: The VC lot and yard figures (116-294, 116-295) were not read.

value.name: Quarters of a household employee, caretaker or watchman
value.conditions: An accessory use on the same lot as a permitted principal use. For a household employee, caretaker or watchman only.
value.note: The code does not say whether the quarters may be a full dwelling unit with a kitchen. Ask the Zoning Officer.

zoning_districts.note: In the Conservation Design Overlay, Option One subdivisions only.

building_types.note: The overlay permits single-family detached dwellings (116-272A).

historic_bypass.note: Historic accessory buildings over 75 years old may exceed the floor area limits and need not meet setbacks, but stay inside the Option One rule.

value.condition: The lot is in an Option One conservation design subdivision in the Conservation Design Overlay (AAAA or AAA), with a permanent conservation easement.

A new structure for the ADU only 'on tracts 15 acres or larger'. Tract area is 'All land area within the site as defined by the deed' (116-11). Two readings: the test is on the whole tract of the Option One subdivision, so a smaller lot in it may qualify, or on the lot's own deed. Ask the Zoning Officer.

When a dwelling is occupied by more than one family, or by adults not of the principal family, the owner or lessee gets an annual occupancy permit, filed by April 1 each year. An accessory structure may be occupied only while the house is occupied.
A restrictive conservation easement on the property prohibits enlarging the ADU, more ADUs than allowed and further subdivision before building permits issue.
Montgomery County Department of Health approval for any on-site sewage disposal system the ADU needs.
All performance and dimensional standards for a primary dwelling unit are met. The ADU is on the same lot as the house, not on its own lot.
A unit in an existing building must be in an existing historic structure.

Steep slopes, in every district (116-169B as amended by Ord. No. 1049, 2026-01-08): on parts of a lot sloped 15% to 25% at most 25% of that area may be regraded, stripped of vegetation or otherwise disturbed; 25% to 35% at most 10%; over 35% no disturbance. An existing improved lot in AAAA to B is exempt from 116-169A only for improvements up to 1% of the lot and 200 sq ft on ground under 15%. Ask the Township Engineer where a new unit or addition would sit.

types_allowed.note: 'The ADU may be located within the principle dwelling, in an existing historic structure or, on tracts 15 acres or larger, in a new structure.'

types_not_addressed.note: An addition and a unit over a garage are not named.

value.detached_new: In a new structure, on a tract of 15 acres or more

max_sqft.note: 'The gross floor area in the first ADU shall not exceed 900 square feet.' The cap is held per form, because historic accessory buildings over 75 years old may exceed it.

max_sqft_by_form.note: First ADU 900 sq ft gross floor area. A unit in an existing historic structure takes 900 sq ft too, unless it is a historic accessory building over 75 years old, which may exceed it. A second ADU 750 sq ft (1,800 on lots over 15 acres).

value.what: an existing historic accessory building more than 75 years old

exempt_building.note: An existing historic accessory building more than 75 years old may be used as an ADU even if it is over the floor area limits, and need not meet the setbacks. The 25 ft ADU height limit does not apply to historic buildings.

max_height_ft.note: 'Any ADU permitted under this subsection shall be limited to a height of 25 feet, with the exception of historic buildings.' The 25 ft is held as a condition for a new structure, so it is not shown for a historic building.

value.where: in a new structure (not a historic building)
value.note: Historic buildings are exempt from the 25 ft limit.

value.where: in a new structure in an AAA Option One subdivision
value.note: Conflicting text, ask. The AAA Option One standards set 20 ft for an accessory building, the ADU rule 25 ft. 116-268C says the more restrictive applies (20 ft). 116-33.2 says overlay requirements take precedence over the underlying district (25 ft).

setback_side_ft.note: 'A completely detached accessory building may occupy a required side and rear yard, but shall not be located closer than four feet to any side or rear lot line.'

separation_ft.note: 'No point on a completely detached accessory building ... shall be any closer than 15 feet to any point on the nearest principal building.'

front_yard_barred.note: Detached accessory buildings: not in the front yard or forward of the front of the house (116-24D(3), E(3)).

family_only.note: 'Including, but not limited to, elder cottages for relatives and tenant houses for employees of a farm or estate.'

max_adus.note: One ADU on a lot under 10 acres in an Option One subdivision, two on a lot of 10 acres or more.

spaces_required.note: No ADU row. 'Dwelling: 2 per dwelling unit (single family, townhome, attached square feet)'. The ADU is a dwelling unit by definition (116-11).

total_on_site.note: Two for the house and two for the ADU.

new_connection_required.note: Only on-site sewage approval by the County Health Department is named.
